# Module `lune_ui_core::playback`

[API reference](../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core`](index.md)

Scripted input in app time: a [`Script`](playback.md#struct.Script) of timed touch gestures, marks and raw events, and a
[`Player`](playback.md#struct.Player) that hands the due events to the frame through [`RawInput::events`](input.md#structfield.RawInput.events), for demos,
recordings and tests that must not depend on the frame rate (D415).

A script is built with a cursor: each gesture starts where the previous one ended and moves the
cursor to its own end. A gesture expands at build time into [`Event::Touch`](input.md#variant.Event.Touch) samples every
[`SAMPLE`](playback.md#constant.SAMPLE), so the events are the same whatever rate the app draws at; a 60 Hz app sees the last
sample of each frame, as it does for a finger. Nothing here reads a clock: the app passes its
time to [`Player::advance`](playback.md#method.Player.advance), which appends the events due by then and returns the marks passed
and the time the player needs the next frame at (give it to
[`Ui::request_repaint_at`](ui.md#method.Ui.request_repaint_at)).

The marks are returned in the same call as the events up to them. An app calls
[`Player::advance`](playback.md#method.Player.advance) before [`Ui::begin`](ui.md#method.Ui.begin), so the frame that follows reads
those events and the state after that frame's draw reflects them: check what a mark names
there, on the frame it passes.

[`draw_touches`](playback.md#fn.draw_touches) draws a disc under each scripted contact, for a recording; it is opt-in and is
written with public painter calls only, so an app could draw its own.

```
use std::time::Duration;
use lune_ui_core::playback::{Player, Script};

let mut script = Script::new();
script.tap((20.0, 30.0)).wait(Duration::from_millis(200)).mark("after the tap");
let mut player = Player::new(script);
let mut events = Vec::new();
let adv = player.advance(Duration::from_secs(1), &mut events);
assert_eq!(events.len(), 1); // the press; the lift is 80 ms later
assert!(adv.next.is_some());
```

<a id="struct.Player"></a>
### Struct `Player`

```rust
pub struct Player {
    // some fields omitted
}
```

Plays a [`Script`](playback.md#struct.Script) against the app's time. It latches its start at the first
[`Self::advance`](playback.md#method.Player.advance), not at construction, so a first frame that comes late starts the script
when it comes.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/playback.rs:258`

**Methods and associated items**

`impl Player`

- <a id="method.Player.advance"></a>`pub fn advance(&mut self, now: Duration, events: &mut Vec<Event>) -> Advance`

  Appends the events due at app time `now` to `events`, in script order, and returns the
  marks passed. The first call starts the script at `now`. While paused, or when `now` is
  earlier than the last call's, nothing is appended. A repeating script that wraps first
  cancels any contact still down, then goes on with the next cycle's cues due by `now`; a
  call that finds whole cycles past skips them rather than replay them in one frame.

- <a id="method.Player.contacts"></a>`pub fn contacts(&self, now: Duration) -> Vec<Contact>`

  The contacts the player emitted that are down, or lifted less than [`FADE`](playback.md#constant.FADE) before `now`,
  each at its last position.

- <a id="method.Player.is_finished"></a>`pub fn is_finished(&self) -> bool`

  Whether a script that does not repeat has played to its end.

- <a id="method.Player.new"></a>`pub fn new(script: Script) -> Self`

  A player of `script`, not yet started.

- <a id="method.Player.pause"></a>`pub fn pause(&mut self, now: Duration)`

  Stops the script's clock at app time `now`: [`Self::advance`](playback.md#method.Player.advance) appends nothing until
  [`Self::resume`](playback.md#method.Player.resume), and the time spent paused is not played back.

- <a id="method.Player.resume"></a>`pub fn resume(&mut self, now: Duration)`

  Starts the clock again at app time `now`: every later cue comes as late as the pause was
  long, so a background of any length replays no burst.

- <a id="method.Player.with_repeat"></a>`pub fn with_repeat(self, repeat: bool) -> Self`

  Whether the script wraps after [`Script::length`](playback.md#method.Script.length) and plays again. The app decides what a
  restart resets ([`Advance::restarted`](playback.md#structfield.Advance.restarted)).

A list of timed cues built by a cursor: touch gestures, raw events and named marks. Each
builder method starts at the cursor and returns `&mut Self`, so calls chain.

## Functions

<a id="fn.draw_touches"></a>
### Function `draw_touches`

```rust
pub fn draw_touches(ui: &mut Ui<'_>, player: &Player)
```

Draws a disc under each of the player's contacts, 44 points across: the theme's `fg_primary`
at 22 % with a 1.5 point ring at 55 %, times the contact's alpha. A lifted contact fades over
[`FADE`](playback.md#constant.FADE) at [`MotionTier::Full`](motion.md#variant.MotionTier.Full) and is gone at once under any lower tier. It shows scripted
contacts only; a live finger is the OS's own setting. It draws on [`LayerId::Toast`](scene.md#variant.LayerId.Toast) with
[`Painter::on`](paint.md#method.Painter.on), which keeps the clip stack, so call it last in a
frame at the top level, outside any clip. It asks for no frame: [`Advance::next`](playback.md#structfield.Advance.next) carries the
end of the fade.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/playback.rs:494`
